harnessChangelog.1.9.0: The construct parser of loss-breakdown.mjs blanks comments before it reads a line: HTML comments in templates and inline templates, and TypeScript comments with the compiler's scanner. A link mifos had commented out (view-collateral.component.html:72) and a sentence of a bitwarden comment that names router.navigate were counted as constructs; the extractor reads neither, so the first was a loss no rule could explain and stopped the fin run, and the second sat in the denominator. Figures this moves: the construct totals of bitwarden (132 to 131) and mifos (1344 to 1343), and everything divided by them. must-context.mjs names every condition the extractor's readers can return, three of which it did not ('superseded by a later navigation', 'in a helper function', 'lazy container'), so the ledger stopped instead of filing a construct under one of them. Measured against the extractor at c8eec9b, which reads a navigation as superseded wherever code after it may navigate, and reverts the round-four regressions.
harnessChangelog.1.8.0: Sixth-round corrections, from a panel run against the re-measured draft. The witness check now judges every source location an edge cites, not only the first: the extractor files the second and later citations of an identical edge under mergedWitnesses, and those were never opened, so a third of the evidence the must tier rests on went unread and four real target mismatches in bitwarden were invisible. The loss table prints a row for every tally key the classifier can emit and refuses to write unless its rows sum to the construct total, after a renamed key had printed zero for a class with members and left 186 constructs unaccounted for. The recovery table prints conversions out of classes in neither of its two groups, which were dropped from both the table and its own All row. compare.mjs writes its tables only after its closure assertion has passed, since writing as it built meant the refusal fired after the good file had already been replaced, and it refuses two runs that name different extractor commits, which is what RQ3 is defined over. to-latex.mjs refuses a raw route file with no comparison block instead of printing its unmatched count as zero and reducing the corpus node total. diagnose-attribution.mjs resolves the adapter from source beside itself rather than from a build path from one machine, and the generators that read a run directory print the extractor commit, the harness version and the label they came from. In the extractor: a canActivate element that is a call is read by its callee and any element that still cannot be named gates the edge anyway, because refusing to read a guard must never be the reason an edge is called deterministic -- bitwarden guards its root with redirectGuard() and fourteen deterministic edges pointed at it; and a `this` parameter is no longer counted when selecting the argument a wrapper files in its children, which shifted the index by one.
harnessChangelog.1.7.0: Third and fourth-round corrections to the independent route parser, every one of them a blind spot it shared with the extractor or a defect a panel reproduced against it. A type-only import is no longer a module edge. Root tables are marked per ARRAY, from the argument of either registration API resolved through the name it is written as, in place of a file-level forRoot test that answered true 0 times in 698 evaluations. Which table in a file a lazy prefix mounts is decided by the member the loadChildren names, else the array RouterModule.forChild registers, else the only table, else none and the subtree is declared unread. A table handed to a helper call or chosen by a conditional is read, and both arms of a conditional are kept out of the root scan. An array registered at the root keeps its root mount whatever claims its file. A route on a named outlet, and everything beneath it, is no longer read at a primary address. A table nested inside an arm the build mounts nowhere is declared once at the construct that selects rather than once more per nesting. Figures this moves: alfresco's declared set 28 to 26 and its coverage back to 100 percent, mifos's declared set 610 to 605 and its blind spots 3 to 1, and every round-two figure derived from them. The agreement between the two readers is now exact on all six applications, which is a weaker form of evidence than it was: a rule either of them gains from the other's reading cannot be a witness to it, so the chapter states the runtime check as the external one.
harnessChangelog.1.6.0: Fourth-round corrections, after a panel reproduced three false findings that all had one shape: a route the tools could not read is indistinguishable from a route the application does not declare, and the census was crediting the difference to the application. The extractor now counts a `matcher:` route as a declared path it cannot read, so the incomplete-route-set note fires for ghostfolio -- which mounts /admin/users with a UrlMatcher, the screen the thesis had published as its one hand-confirmed dead link. It follows a `{ path: '**', component: X }` catch-all as well as the redirecting flavour, which is the flavour both applications the surviving count comes from actually use. It resolves tsconfig `paths` aliases, so alfresco's /nodes/:nodeId/rules subtree is visible to both tools instead of being minted at the project root. writtenNames reads a quoted or computed Object.assign key by its value and treats every assignment operator and an aliased `this` as a write, closing five more ways a reassigned field drew a must edge to its initializer's target. stripI18nMeta now walks Angular's own findEndOfBlock. In the oracle: Storybook fixture route arrays are no longer read as declared screens, and a screen whose path expression could not be resolved becomes SCREEN_UNRESOLVED -- recorded and reported as a blind spot, but outside the coverage denominator, because a verbatim expression is not an address. unexplained.mjs tests the whole commands array as a route pattern rather than its first segment, and gives a target inside an unreadable subtree and a relative target with no base their own reasons instead of counting both as a dead link. notes.mjs reads the notes out of the db the map run wrote rather than re-extracting them, and run-all.mjs drives it and unexplained.mjs, writes the <slug>.<label>.*.json files round2-to-latex.mjs reads, and exits non-zero when unexplained.mjs does. What that reproduces depends on the extractor it builds. The pinned sha is the pre-attribution parent (see extractor.note) and predates the round-two fixes, so it reproduces none of the published figures: the RQ1 to RQ4 figures need the thesis-eval tag, and the Section 5.5 figures need the round-two extractor, each passed with --extractor-dir (--label ctrl against the extractor as it stood before the round, --label fin against the round-two one, into one --out). RQ1 to RQ3 figures come from harness 1.2.0 and the RQ4 figures from 1.3.0, and no 1.6.0 change was applied to any of them.
harnessChangelog.1.5.0: Third-round corrections to the dead-link finding, after a panel showed the second round had counted it from the wrong population. The extractor no longer withholds a wildcard edge when a declared path is unreadable --- Angular forwards the URL either way --- and instead emits one incomplete-route-set note per application and writes that caveat into every wildcard note from it, so no consumer may call a link dead while the route set is a lower bound. notes.mjs added, which dumps the extractor's soundiness notes unfiltered; witness-check.mjs now writes mustBad, the must-tier violations the thesis describes one by one, which findings alone does not isolate. round2-to-latex.mjs counts dead-link candidates only where the target names a path (not the application root, not an unresolved relative target) and the application's route set is complete. RQ1 to RQ3 figures come from 1.2.0 and the RQ4 figures from 1.3.0, and none is affected.
harnessChangelog.1.4.0: Second-round corrections, all of them blind spots the oracle shared with the extractor: a route path resolved through a constant, an enum or Angular $localize; a first-party import resolved against tsconfig baseUrl and paths; a route array named rather than written out, and one reached through a barrel re-export or a loadChildren that references its module directly; Angular relative-link semantics in witness-check (a template routerLink is route-relative, navigate only with relativeTo); loss-breakdown reports excluded/inScope and counts an unknown-modality or unplaced-source witness as accounted rather than converted; unexplained.mjs added, which fails when any unrecovered site has no reason. RQ1 to RQ3 figures come from 1.2.0 and the RQ4 figures from 1.3.0, and none is affected.
harnessChangelog.1.3.0: mutate.mjs only; RQ1 to RQ3 figures from 1.2.0 are unaffected. Patches the source at the matched offset instead of by string content (a string replace always hit the first identical construct); judges detection at witness level as well as edge level; retargets CHANGE_NAV_TARGET to a declared route; excludes guard mutants on screens no edge enters; seeded stratified sampling with a fixed quota per operator; reports detection per operator with n.
harnessChangelog.1.2.0: route parser corrections, tier-aware witness check, per-construct conversion.

The figures were produced by two runs of run-all.mjs over this commit, with the attribution pass disabled and enabled.
